note: The web smoke fails when the night's load (Play to a running night) divided by the same run's load to the menu, floored at menu_floor_s, is over max_ratio, or when the night alone is over ceiling_s (a backstop for a hang). Re-derived for issue #966 from the 181 web-smoke artifacts of the runs of 3 and 4 Nov 2026 (main and pull requests; the headless shell, SwiftShader, 1280x720): night 25.0 to 95.1 s (median 52.9), menu 8.2 to 18.0 s (median 14.9), night over max(menu, 14) 1.8 to 6.8 (median 3.2). The first calibration (28 runs, 5.5 over a floor of 8 s) failed 8 of these 181 healthy runs, and three pull requests whose menu loaded in 7 to 9 s (the night over the menu rose, the night did not). The floor sits at the usual menu, so a faster menu no longer raises the gate; the limit is 10 % over the worst of the 181. The night is not predicted by the menu (log correlation 0.58), nor by the idle menu frame (0.51), nor by the running night's frame time (0.71): the same build takes 3.8 times as long on the slowest run as on the fastest, so whatever the divisor, a time gate passing every healthy run cannot see less than about a doubling (a night x1.5 fails 4 % of the replayed runs, x2 30 %, x3 82 %). A growth that is not that large is held by a count that does not move with the runner: tests/night/test_load_cost.gd (frames the warm-up draws, seconds of sound decoded, lit shaders). Replay: python -I tools/web_smoke/night_load.py --scale 1.5 <result.json>... Issues #873 and #966.
